tldr: Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash undercut Claude and GPT on price using domestic chips in late August, and Anthropic answered Sep 2 with a 75% cache-price cut and 70% more output tokens on Fable/Mythos 5.1. T. Rowe Price then publicized broad Claude adoption across its investment process on Sep 10.
whats_new: Anthropic shipped Claude Opus 5.5 on Sep 22, and about an hour later OpenAI answered with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna -- Simon Willison frames the same-day releases as a new price war, not just a capability race.
why_it_matters: Same-day flagship launches from both labs mean whichever pricing and rate limits you pinned evals to last week may already be stale -- check current price sheets before trusting last month's cost comparisons.

open_questions: Do Claude Opus 5.5's and GPT-6 Sol/Luna's posted prices actually beat GLM-5.3-Flash's domestic-chip pricing, or just each other?
Are GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna two distinct price/capability tiers, or two names for closely related releases?
Is T. Rowe Price's adoption driven by pricing, capability, or compliance advantages -- and are other regulated-industry customers making the same call?
take_for_builders: Re-price your Claude vs. GPT cost model now that Opus 5.5 and Sol/Luna are both live -- don't assume last month's per-token numbers still hold, and re-check T. Rowe Price's case study only as a vendor-risk data point, not a pricing signal.
